core_obligations: Write down the short exact sequence of complexes 0 to I tensor K(A, g) to K(A, g) to K(A/I, g) to 0 (proof lines 7480-7485).

Use the hypothesis that the images of the g_j in A/I are H_1-regular to conclude that the complex on the right has vanishing H_1, and hence that the induced map on the degree-one cokernels is injective (proof lines 7486-7492).
Identify the two cokernels with A/(g_1, ..., g_m) and I/I(g_1, ..., g_m) and translate injectivity into the identity I cap (g_1, ..., g_m) = I(g_1, ..., g_m) (proof lines 7492-7493).
proof_roadmap: Interval comparison against the 57 public records of more-algebra.tex: no recorded interval covers 7471-7494. The nearest records are 340 (7359-7438, tag 062I) and 341 (8259-8332, tag 07CZ); public 340 relates first Koszul homology regularity to quasi-regularity and is the closest in vocabulary, but it is a different statement about equivalent regularity notions rather than about an intersection of ideals with a sequence.
difficulty_reason: The lemma computes an intersection of ideals under a regularity hypothesis: if the images of g_1 to g_m in A/I form an H_1-regular sequence, then I cap (g_1, ..., g_m) equals I times (g_1, ..., g_m) (statement lines 7471-7476). The proof is short but has real content (proof lines 7479-7494): it forms the standard short exact sequence of Koszul complexes attached to the surjection A to A/I, uses the vanishing of H_1 of the right hand complex, which is exactly the hypothesis, to read off injectivity of the induced map on the degree-one cokernels, and then identifies that injectivity statement with the asserted identity of ideals. The identification in the last step is where a reader has to work: the two cokernels are A^m to A and I^m to I, and their kernels are exactly (g_1, ..., g_m) and I(g_1, ..., g_m).
